source: Kiyokawa and Dienes (2019) Effects of verbalization toward self or other on insight problem solving (CogSci, preregistration of exploratory study); reports Schooler et al. 1993 Exp 3 and Gilhooly et al. 2010
finding: Gives the headline numbers of Schooler, Ohlsson and Brooks (1993) Exp 3 as reported secondhand, plus a tighter replication that did not find the insight-specific cost, plus a new small T-puzzle study that leans toward a cost.
numbers: Schooler 1993 Exp 3 (secondhand): verbalizing cut problems solved in 6 min by 25% for insight and about 5% for non-insight (interaction 20%). Gilhooly, Fioratou and Henretty 2010 (4 min): insight 57 vs 53% (verbal vs silent), non-insight 48 vs 48%, interaction F=1.63 n.s.; Bayes factor 0.92 (insensitive, neither for nor against). Kiyokawa and Dienes T-puzzle N=34: solved 3/11 toward-self, 5/12 toward-other, 8/11 control; verbalize vs control OR=5.0, 95% CI 1.03 to 24.29. Earlier Kiyokawa and Nakazawa 2006 OR=3.11.
quote: the evidence favoured a detrimental verbalization effect rather than an overall positive effect of verbalization
limits: Schooler 1993 figures are secondhand; the original PDF was not retrievable (site redirected). Original per-experiment N and F values remain unknown. Non-significant replications can be insensitive, so the replication status is mixed, not refuted. T-puzzle study is tiny and exploratory.
agent_relevance: The verbal-cost effect for insight is real in some tasks and absent in others; do not hard-code 'never explain' or 'always explain'. Treat rationale on or off as a task-class switch tested per item type.

source: Deng, Brucks and Toubia (2026) A Cognitive Framework for Idea Diversity in Large Language Models (arXiv 2602.20408v2)
finding: LLM idea sets are less diverse than human sets. Ordinary-person persona modifiers restore diversity between ideators but raise fixation within one session. Chain-of-thought reduces that fixation. Both together give the highest diversity, above humans on one metric. Temperature barely helps.
numbers: Study 1: 99 Prolific humans vs 99 simulated GPT-4o participants (temp 1.0), 10 fitness-product ideas each. Pooled categories: human 28 vs LLM 23; unique category combinations human 208 vs LLM 89. Study 2 (83 per cell, 830 ideas): LLM default 23 categories / 85 combos; LLM + CoT 27 / 152; ordinary personas + CoT 27 / 240; humans 28 / 196 (human + CoT 28 / 184). Temperature 1.0 to 1.5 on 990 ideas: categories 22 to 23, combos 89 to 97; temp 2.0 incoherent. First-idea combos per 10: human 8.99 vs LLM default 5.98. Replicated with gemini-3.1-pro-preview and gpt-5.6-sol; the partitioning gap shrinks in the newer model.
quote: Temperature does not close the human-LLM diversity gap and can impair output quality
limits: One task domain (fitness products), categories labelled by an LLM, ideas judged by category not quality or usefulness. Persona and CoT effects measured per condition, not at an equal-token budget; CoT uses extra tokens.
agent_relevance: Best direct operator evidence: change who is thinking (ordinary personas) and force a short plan before each idea. This is a cheap variation operator with measured gain; temperature is not.

source: Zhang et al. (2025) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity (arXiv 2510.01171)
finding: Asking the model to list several answers with their stated probabilities in one call raises diversity far more than asking for one answer. It works without training and stacks with top-p and min-p. Larger models gain more.
numbers: Creative writing (poems, jokes, stories): diversity up by 1.6 to 2.1 times over direct prompting; human rating +25.7%; recovers 66.8% of the base model's diversity; larger models (GPT-4.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro) gain 1.5 to 2 times more than smaller ones (GPT-4.1-Mini, Gemini-2.5-Flash). Factual accuracy and safety not harmed in their ablations.
limits: Authors' own results, diversity measured with their own metrics; one call produces k answers so token cost per distinct answer differs from k independent calls. No insight or reasoning-accuracy task.
agent_relevance: A cheap operator to widen the first sample pool: one call, many stated candidates. Fits the wide-cheap-sampling stage of an explicit-implicit loop.

source: Nguyen, Tschiatschek and Singla (2026) Enhancing Diversity of LLM-Generated Educational Tasks (CreativeDC, arXiv 2512.23601v2)
finding: A two-stage prompt (explore the creative space first, then satisfy the requirements) gives more distinct high-utility tasks than a plain prompt or 'think step by step'. Plain CoT is no better than the base prompt.
numbers: Qwen3-235B-A22B, temp 1.0. At K=50 tasks: CreativeDC about 13 distinct tasks (about 12 among high-utility) by Vendi score vs about 8 for both CoT and BASE; p<0.001 Bonferroni-corrected paired Wilcoxon; CoT vs BASE not different. Experts found about 16 clusters for CreativeDC. About 1.6 times more distinct high-utility tasks.
limits: One model, one domain (Python teaching tasks), three expert raters. Compares prompts, not equal-token budgets; the two-stage prompt writes more.
agent_relevance: Shows divergent-then-convergent structure beats generic 'think step by step' for variety, a small direct test of the explicit-implicit idea (explore wide, then check against rules).

source: Zhang et al. (2025) NoveltyBench: Evaluating Language Models for Humanlike Diversity (arXiv 2504.05228)
finding: 20 leading models give fewer distinct answers than humans. Larger models in a family are often less diverse. In-context regeneration (ask for a different answer with prior answers visible) is the strongest simple operator and can match human writers; paraphrase and a creativity system prompt do little.
numbers: Temperature 1, 10 samples per prompt: many leading models give fewer than 3 distinct answers in 10; smaller models (Gemma 2-2B, Llama 3.2-1B) most diverse. On 100 curated prompts with Claude-3 Opus, GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0 Pro over 8 generations: in-context regeneration roughly matched human writers (8 authors); GPT-4o and Gemini 2.0 Pro beat human cumulative utility. Equivalence classifier 79% accuracy vs human labels (F1 reported), human-label agreement 85% in another check.
limits: Human baseline is 8 paper authors; classifier-based distinctness; open-ended prompts, not reasoning problems.
agent_relevance: Operator ranking for variation: keep earlier candidates in context and ask for a different one, beats sampling and paraphrase. Dedup by meaning, not by string.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs (arXiv 2412.21187)
finding: In o1-like models the first solution round already holds the correct answer in the large majority of solved cases. Later rounds mostly re-check. This is the closest LLM analog to the human fast-first-answer finding.
numbers: QwQ-32B-Preview and DeepSeek-R1 on ASDIV and MATH500: first round gives the correct answer in more than 92% of cases (about 97% QwQ on ASDIV; 89 to 93% on other cells); first round is under 60% of tokens (QwQ ASDIV: 287 tokens, 38.7% of response). Simple 2+3 question: o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens than conventional models. Streamlining cut tokens by 48.6% on MATH500 with accuracy kept.
limits: Math word problems with a checkable answer, two open models, not insight riddles. Counts first correct appearance, not whether the model endorses it.
agent_relevance: Supports O: keep the first-sample candidate and stop early on easy items. It does not show the same for insight items, which are rarer in this data.

source: Laban, Hayashi, Zhou and Neville (2025) LLMs Get Lost in Multi-Turn Conversation (arXiv 2505.06120)
finding: Models do worse when a problem arrives in pieces. They make early assumptions and do not recover from a wrong turn. Restating everything in a fresh single turn helps only partly. A kind of restart test.
numbers: Average drop of 39% from single to multi-turn across six tasks, 200,000+ simulated conversations; mostly a rise in unreliability, with a small loss of aptitude. A final recap turn or gradual snowball repeat recovers only 15 to 20% of the loss for GPT-4o; unreliability stays about 30% even at temperature 0 for both user and assistant.
limits: Not a creativity or incubation study. The recap keeps the old wrong turns in context; it is not a clean fresh-context restart with the question alone.
agent_relevance: Indirect: a wrong early commitment stays in the context. Fresh-context restart should carry only the question and the surviving constraints, not the failed attempt; no direct LLM incubation test exists.

source: Snell, Lee, Xu and Kumar (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters (arXiv 2408.03314)
finding: At equal test-time compute, sequential revision beats parallel sampling on easy problems, and parallel sampling or search wins on hard problems that need different high-level approaches. A mix with an ideal ratio is best.
numbers: Compute-optimal strategy beats best-of-N using about 4x less test-time compute; on questions where a small model can match, test-time compute can beat a 14x larger model. Ideal sequential-to-parallel ratio depends on question difficulty (MATH, PaLM-2 based, learned verifier).
limits: Math with learned verifiers; not insight items. 'Hard' here means low pass rate, not need for restructuring.
agent_relevance: Gives the equal-token comparison form the gap asks for, in math. Hints that wide independent sampling (explicit-implicit split) should be used when the problem needs a different approach, and plain revising when it is nearly right.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling (arXiv 2407.21787)
finding: The share of problems solved by any sample rises log-linearly with sample count over four orders of magnitude. With an automatic verifier this turns into real accuracy. Without one, majority vote and reward models plateau beyond several hundred samples.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite with DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Instruct: 15.9% with one sample to 56% with 250 samples, beating the single-sample state of the art 43%. Voting and reward-model selection plateau after a few hundred samples.
limits: Domains with checkable answers; insight riddles lack a cheap exact verifier. Coverage is an upper bound, not accuracy.
agent_relevance: Direct support for the wide-sampling plus rule-check design: the gain depends on the check being reliable. Where no check exists, extra samples stop paying.

source: Sprague et al. (2024/2025) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning (arXiv 2409.12183)
finding: Meta-analysis of over 100 papers plus own tests on 20 datasets and 14 models: CoT helps mainly when the task is math or symbolic; elsewhere gains are near zero.
numbers: Mean CoT gain: symbolic reasoning 14.2, math 12.3, logical reasoning 6.9 points. Top three categories average 56.9 with CoT vs 45.5 without; other categories 56.8 vs 56.1. On MMLU CoT ~ direct unless the question or response contains an equals sign.
limits: Mostly 2023-2024 models and published papers (publication bias). Gain measured as accuracy only; no insight or creativity category tested separately.
agent_relevance: Gives the task-class rule for rationale: use on math and symbolic items, make it optional elsewhere. Combined with Liu 2025 harm on implicit-pattern tasks, drop the rationale for pattern and recognition items.

source: Gema et al. (2025) Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute (arXiv 2507.14417, TMLR)
finding: Giving reasoning models longer reasoning budgets lowers accuracy on some task types, with different failure modes per model family: Claude models become more distracted by irrelevant information, OpenAI o-series overfit to problem framing, all lose focus on long constraint tracking.
numbers: Task categories: counting with distractors, regression with spurious features, deduction with constraint tracking, advanced AI-risk probes. Five failure modes listed in the abstract. Per-model accuracy curves vs token budget not extracted by me.
limits: Tasks hand-built to expose the effect; only abstract-level reading plus the figure overview this session.
agent_relevance: Current-model evidence that more written thinking can hurt; supports a budget cap and a dropped-rationale path on distractor-heavy or spurious-pattern items.

source: Search result summary: Creative Problem Solving in Large Language and Vision Models: What Would it Take? (arXiv 2405.01453)
finding: Position paper that describes Wallas stages including incubation and says prior machine work does not cover incubation for LLMs or vision-language models.
limits: Seen through a search snippet only. Used only to support the claim that no published LLM incubation experiment was found by search; two search engines and the arXiv API (rate-limited) were consulted.
agent_relevance: Gap 2 stays open: incubation is only a design idea for LLMs, not a tested operator.

source: Search result summary: Kumar et al. (2025) Human Creativity in the Age of LLMs (arXiv 2410.03703, CHI 2025)
finding: Humans helped by an LLM did better in assisted tasks but not better afterwards in unassisted tasks; this is exposure then delay then test, on people, not model-side incubation.
agent_relevance: Not evidence for LLM incubation; shows the delay design exists for humans.

source: Mizumoto et al. (2025) NazoNazo riddles (arXiv 2509.14704), re-read for the endorsement gap
finding: Same study as b13, re-opened only to answer Gap 8: right candidates appear in thought logs but are not endorsed; no external verifier was tested in the paper, so whether a verifier closes the human gap is not known from it.
numbers: As in b13: reasoning models 17.6%, non-reasoning 7.6%, humans 52.9%.
limits: No verifier ablation found in this read; I did not find another published verifier test on insight riddles.
agent_relevance: The failure is in the final endorsement step, so an external rule check or second-sample vote is the natural fix, but it is untested on insight riddles.

source: Cross-check of d01 with prior b03/b20/K22: Schooler and Engstler-Schooler face overshadowing registered replication (already in b20)
finding: Search summary: critics say Schooler 1993 insight problems were mostly spatial and the non-insight problems mostly verbal, a confound; Ericsson and Simon noted the verbalization instructions were non-standard; Fleck and Weisberg 2003/2004 found no effect on the candle problem.
limits: Search-result summary only, not the primary text.
agent_relevance: Reason to treat the insight-specific verbal cost as unsettled; supports task-class not blanket rule.

finding: No paper was found that tests an explicit-implicit (EII) two-stage LLM scaffold against a plain loop at equal tokens on insight items; none on program-triggered reframing with frontier models beyond d'Aliberti; Weisberg 2015 and Fleck and Weisberg 2013 full texts were not retrievable (search budget exhausted, API rate limits).
limits: A negative from limited search. Closest proxies are d04, d08 and d09 which test related structures on other tasks.
agent_relevance: The experiment is worth running in our own bench; use Snell-style equal-token arms.
